text:
maya: heads up — noticed a weird pattern in the latest rollout for rwd-v5 -> v5-int4. holdout slice showing a 1.9% absolute F1 drop, but online perf (latency/cost) looks fine. canary promoted ~2h ago. :eyes:
liam: hmm — what slice? full corpus or a specific domain? any sample diffs?
maya: mainly "docs-longform" and "summaries_high_density" slices. sample size ~5k requests in 2h. distribution shift looks small but token-level hallucination count rose on those slices.
deploy-bot: promotion event: model=rwd-v5 variant=v5-int4 promoted to 10% traffic by orchestrator at 1718499800. autoscale unchanged.
jorge: can you paste the eval query / metric pull? also did shadow compare show this before promote? :thinking_face:
maya: here are the quick pulls i ran:
```
SELECT slice, metric, pre_mean, post_mean, delta_abs
FROM rollout_metrics
WHERE model='rwd-v5' AND variant='v5-int4'
  AND window IN ('2h_pre','2h_post')
  AND metric IN ('f1','halluc_rate')
```
results: docs-longform f1 0.842 -> 0.823 (delta -0.019), halluc_rate 0.012 -> 0.029 (delta +0.017)
liam: that halluc jump is concerning. did quantization config use per-channel qscale or the fallback mixed-precision path?
maya: we used int4-nf4 + per-channel calibration. no mixed fallback.
srijan: two quick checks: 1) confirm KV cache behavior for long context on int4 path, 2) check beam/search config parity with baseline. Sometimes decoding prunes differ post-quant.
jorge: agree. also check the prefix-caching hit rate for those slices — if cache misses spike, model will generate from scratch more often and hallucinate more.
maya: running cache-hit slice now. also attaching 10 sample pairs (pre vs post) — pasted in thread (private).
liam: what are our auto-fallback thresholds again? iirc we have canyon: absolute F1 drop >1.5% on any critical slice OR halluc_rate increase >0.01 -> automatic rollback at 5% traffic.
jorge: correct. but the automatic runner only triggers if the delta persists for 30m with p<0.05 on bootstrap test. current window is ~2h since promote but we need persistence check.
maya: ok—i can trigger a quick 0% pause and reduce to 1% while we debug. thoughts?
srijan: do that. also spin a shadow run of quant-int8 with same config to see if quant level is the issue. if int8 matches baseline then int4 is suspect.
liam: I can allocate a small dedicated pool to replay the failing sample slice on int8 vs int4. ping me when you have the list.
maya: doing the pause now — reducing variant to 1% at 1718500200. will run replay and post logs. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: traffic update: variant=v5-int4 -> 1% at 1718500200 per user action maya.
jorge: thanks. one more ask — capture token-level logits for a few hallucination cases, we want to inspect top-k stability differences.
maya: noted. collecting logits and decoder traces, will upload to the eval bucket.
srijan: once we have replay + logits, we'll run the smoothed-rollback-checker script and decide next step. if int4 shows consistent regressions we'll mark it on the watchlist and require mixed-precision fallback by default.
liam: also add a quick canary note to the rollout ticket so PMs know rollback occurred. i can update.
maya: thanks all. will follow up with replay results in ~30–45m. :rocket:
